title: Pseudo-coherent complexes of finite Tor dimension are perfect
statement: Let S be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let K be a pseudo-coherent object of D(\mathcal O_S) [def-pc-derived-category, def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex]. If K has finite Tor dimension, then K is perfect [def-pc-perfect-complex].

source.place: Cohomology of Sheaves, Lemma 20.49.5 (Tag 08CQ; label cohomology-lemma-perfect)

proof.text: For each point choose a bounded-above finite-free representative from [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex]. Refine to an affine open V and restrict the complex termwise, preserving the bound and free terms. The derived restriction composition isomorphism transports its representing isomorphism. Lift the differentials through the full faithful affine sheafification functor of [lem-pc-affine-perfect-module-model], using the finite-free tilde comparison [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections]. Faithfulness verifies the shape and square-zero equations. This gives a bounded-above finite-free module complex M and an actual sheaf-complex isomorphism.

The lifted M is pseudo-coherent by its own bounded-above finite-free model. Apply [lem-pc-affine-sheafification-tor-amplitude] to transfer Tor bounds to Q(M), and then [lem-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-finite-tor-perfect] to obtain a bounded finite-projective E with Q(E) isomorphic to Q(M).

Split each finite-projective term of E off a finite free module by Module.Finite.exists_comp_eq_id_of_projective. Affine sheafification preserves the splitting equations, finite-free identifications and zero objects, so it gives a strictly perfect complex in the sense of [def-pc-perfect-complex]. Transport the derived isomorphism through the functor and factorization of [lem-pc-affine-localized-derived-sheafification]. Compose with the original representing isomorphism and use the pointwise definition of perfectness.
